description: SEMA participa en el desafío de Field Shift. Nuestro objetivo es crear una solución digital que convierta datos abiertos de la NASA en información útil para apoyar decisiones agrícolas según la ubicación, el clima y el terreno. Buscamos integrantes responsables con interés en software, análisis, agricultura, ciencias dela tierra e inteligencia articicial.
summary:
SEMA (Space-Based Agricultural Monitoring System) is a digital platform designed to support farmers and agronomists in making better-informed agricultural decisions.

Our solution combines geographic information, NASA POWER climate data, complementary meteorological sources, and farmer-provided information about soil, water availability, and crop history.

The current prototype allows users to explore farmland information, review environmental conditions, and receive preliminary agricultural guidance based on their goals, such as soil improvement, water conservation, and crop diversification.

Built with modern web technologies and a modular approach, SEMA aims to evolve into a scalable, multilingual platform with offline capabilities for rural communities.

Our long-term vision is to provide regionally adapted crop rotation guidance supported by scientific evidence.

SEMA does not seek to replace farmers or agronomists. Instead, it aims to complement their expertise, promote sustainable land management, and make scientific information more accessible worldwide.
details:
SEMA — Space-Based Agricultural Monitoring System

The Problem

Farmers worldwide face challenges related to climate variability, soil degradation, water availability, and agricultural planning. Although valuable scientific and environmental data exist, accessing and interpreting this information can be difficult, particularly for rural communities.

Our Solution

SEMA is a digital agricultural monitoring platform designed to make geographic, climate, and agricultural information more accessible and useful.

The platform allows users to register farmland, explore geographic information, review available environmental data, and provide information about their crops, soil conditions, drainage, irrigation systems, and water availability.

Farmers can select agricultural goals such as improving soil health, conserving water, reducing risks, or diversifying crops.

Our current prototype evaluates the available information, identifies missing variables, and provides preliminary agricultural guidance.

Scientific Foundation and NASA Data

SEMA incorporates climate information from NASA POWER, including temperature, precipitation, and solar radiation, with Open-Meteo as a complementary meteorological source.

These environmental variables help provide context for agricultural analysis.

Our crop rotation approach draws on agronomic principles such as crop diversification, botanical family rotation, soil conservation, and water management.

The next development stage will focus on evaluating crop species according to regional climate, soil characteristics, water availability, and agricultural history.

Technology and Development

SEMA uses React and TypeScript to build an interactive web interface.

Our development workflow includes Git and GitHub for version control and collaboration.

The project follows a modular approach, allowing geographic, climate, and agricultural components to evolve independently.

Python is part of our data-processing and backend development strategy, supporting the goal of expanding scientific data analysis and future agricultural models.

Artificial intelligence tools have also supported development activities, including technical research, coding assistance, debugging, documentation, and translation.

Innovation and Global Scalability

SEMA aims to connect scientific information with practical agricultural needs through a single, understandable platform.

Our long-term vision includes regionally adapted crop guidance, multilingual access, and offline-first capabilities for rural communities with limited connectivity.

The platform is designed to evolve toward supporting different countries, agricultural systems, and environmental conditions.

Expected Impact

SEMA aims to support sustainable agricultural practices, soil conservation, more informed water management, and improved access to environmental information.

By helping farmers understand their land and available data, the project has the potential to support agricultural resilience and food security.

These expected benefits will require further validation through scientific evaluation and testing with agricultural communities.

Human Expertise Comes First

SEMA is not intended to replace farmers or agronomists.

Instead, our goal is to complement their knowledge and experience with accessible scientific information and digital tools.

We believe space-related data and modern software engineering can help address real challenges on Earth and contribute to a more sustainable agricultural future.
